lines.english: "Kazusa."
"Mh, mmmh…"
"Hey, Kazusa… Wake up already."
"Mh, mhh…?"
The sunlight beaming in through the massive high-rise hotel window has already lit up the room thoroughly.
Yet a sleeping beauty remains tucked within her bed amidst the abundant light.
…Though I suppose some things never change no matter what country we're in.
"Fuaaaaah… What time is it?"
"It'll be eleven soon."
Of course, I'm not going to act annoyed or surprised. Kazusa's always like thisーexcept for when she's playing the piano, that is.
"Why would you wake me up so early…? Lemme sleep until lunch."
"I'm already hungry. I want lunch now."
In any case, it's been five hours since I woke up. I'm starting to get bored of looking at her sleep…
"Then call for room service or something."
"No, wake up! We're going to head out soon."
"Where?"
"There is no where."
"What are you, a poet?"
"We're going to enjoy Japan, aren't we? …Did we not promise Youko-san last night?"
I suppose it's tough to say if that can even be considered a promise, though Kazusa didn't seem to oppose the idea at the time, at least.
…But she didn't really agree to it either.
"Let's go to the lounge and discuss where we'll go over lunch, okay? Come on, let's get dressed and…"
"I'm not going. I'll be asleep all day."
"…There's seriously nothing for me to do. I've miraculously managed to wrap up all my work for the year."
"Going out is only going to exhaust me. I'd much rather have your thing… inside my mouth."
"…! That would exhaust you more than going out."
"In any case, I said I'm not going, so you should stay with me, Haruki. Let's watch some lame suspense movie rerun together."
"Don't watch it if you already know it's lame…"
Even when throwing one of her childish tantrums, Kazusa has never once suggested that I go out by myself.
"But I don't have anywhere I want to go, nor anyone I can meet."
"How about catching up with some old friends?"
I wonder if those last words by Youko-san had a specific intention behind them, or if she was simply trying to be sarcastic.
…One thing's for certain though: she didn't mean it simply as a passing remark.
"But, you know… you're…"
You're supposed to have been forgiven.
In Vienna, half a year ago.
By a visitor we never could have imagined would come. During an impossible reunion, and the miraculous reconciliation that followed.
"That doesn't mean…"
"Don't you want to see her?"
"Of course I do! But… I can't take the initiative."
"Kazusa…"
"No matter how much she's willing to forgive me, I can't forgive myself."
"I loved her. I really did admire her."
I'm fully aware of that.
After all, she managed to love someone like me, and yet I…
"How about you, Haruki? Can you bring yourself to meet her?"
"Well, you know…"
I want Kazusa to find salvation. But I myself don't deserve it.
Really, we haven't grown at all even after three years, huh? Not me, and not Kazusa.
"I seem to remember telling you I wanted to remain inside."
"We're just going for a walk. You can tolerate that much, right?"
In the end, it took yet another 30 minutes to drag the grumbling Kazusa outside…
By the time we finished lunch and left the hotel, the faint winter sun had already made its way west.
"What if we run into someone?"
"Just where do you think we are? This is a city of over ten million people in the heart of world-famous Tokyo!
"B-But… you know… last time I came back to Japan, plenty of people recognized me."
"Don't worry, the Touma Kazusa craze is long since over. Don't underestimate how short attention spans Japanese people have."
"Hold on, is that really something my manager should be happy about?"
"Besides, I have a plan. Anyway, accompany me for a while."
"I said no!"
Fully awake and with a full stomach, yet still unwilling to move by herself, Kazusa decides to grab hold of my sleeve and lets herself get dragged along.
But even then, I half-forcibly drag Kazusa with me outside, into Japan.
Because…
"Look, we're here. This'll be our first tourist spot."
"Huh? But this is… just outside our hotel."
"Hey, Kazusa… Do you remember this scenery?"
"Scenery? …This is just the street in front of Onjuku Station…"
"…It's still here, this telephone booth."
"Huh?"
"You ran away from a journalist, and at the same time lost your wallet and your cell phone, along with everything else in your bag."
"The truth is… this number is the only one I remember. What's wrong with me?"
"From this very booth, you called me with a 100 yen coin you found…"
"Wah, wah, wah! I'm going home! I'm going home after all!"
"And with a pitiful voice, like that of an abandoned dog…"
"Y-Your voice was pitiful too!"
"Of course it was. A natural reaction to hearing your pitiful voice."
"When I came for you in a panic, I found you trembling and dripping wet. I thought to myself, wow, she really does look like an abandoned dog."
"Oh that's rich, coming from the owner who abandoned me!"
"Don't make this my fault…"
"I could say the same, you bastard…! Don't try to rile me up, you bastard!"
"I'm only doing it because a certain idiot keeps falling for the same old cliched provocations."
"Only because you're the one saying them, you bastard…"
That's right, I will half-forcibly drag Kazusa with me outside, into Japan.
Because no longer will we sink into an endless cycle of self-indulgence, like we used to back then.
No matter how many punches we have to take, and no matter how hard it is, we'll live in harmony with the outside world.
I've decided to move forward with my life, even if it means I have to get hurt, whether because of myself or because of others.
"Look, there's the mirror."
"I see, this is your 'plan'… Your tastes and methods haven't changed a bit."
"I went for a similar look on purpose."
"How about it… Touno Kazumi-san?"
Fake glasses and a comb as a hair ornament. Then add to that a scarf and a hat.
And not least of all, a fake name.
That's what I gave to Kazusa three years ago, but it's not the only thing I gave her in this place.
The shopping mall within walking distance from the hotel.
The assortments and layouts have changed a little, but all the stores we visited together back then are still here.
"Still, thinking back now, I don't look good in glasses at all."
"Huh, you think so? I think it fits you perfectly, including your hair."
"That's what people call husband's bias. I'm sorry, but I can't take your praise seriously."
"Oh, thanks a lot."
Although thoroughly deriding my opinion, Kazusa looks like she's actually happy about my questionable sense of beauty.
She looks pretty uplifted as she walks ahead of me in the shopping mall, wearing every single accessory I bought for her.
"Hey, Haruki, how about we go eat something sweet? I think they have a Rascal's in the underground mall here."
"We're back in Japan, so how about we take the occasion to grab some zenzai soup or something instead?"
"Alright, that'll be our second destination. Come on, let's hurry."
"No, wait, we don't need to eat everything in succession. There's no shortage of pudding back home in Europe."
"…You're seriously underestimating Rascal's smooth puddings. That exquisite texture is a rarity even in Europe, just so you know."
"Setting aside whether that's actually true or not… It's cold, right? We should go eat something warm."
"That's why I was kind enough to suggest that we make that our second destination! How selfish can you be?"
"I'll toss those exact words right back at you. How about you just buy the puddings and take them home as a souvenir?"
"Not happening. I want to eat them now. I'll never compromise on this. I'll eat three of them in the store, and bring twelve home with me."
"…You won't be able to eat dinner like that."
"I have another stomach for dessert! What are you even on about?"
"…Fine, I've had enough. Do whatever you want."
"Oh right, if we eat ice cream after warming ourselves up with zenzai, then…"
"Why do you insist on making me freeze!?"
She looks pretty uplifted indeed… In fact, she's getting way ahead of herself.
"Hnng… I'm finally in my element. Come on, Haruki!"
"Ugh…"
When we exited the shopping mall into the streets of Onjuku, the dynamic between the two of us was already completely reversed.
"Oh, how pathetic can you be? Did you get an upset tummy from eating that tiny amount?"
"I only feel sick because of a certain ingredient…"
In fact, I'm terrified of what results I'd get if I did a glucose urine test right now.
The same can't be said for Kazusa however. She seems completely fine despite having stuffed herself with twice the amount of sugar that I have.
"H-Hey… how about we go back to the hotel? Let's watch some lame end-of-year special variety shows together."
"Why would you watch something you already know is lame?"
But my plea falls on deaf ears. Without a care in the world about the man pressing his hands against his belly, Kazusa goes onwards on the concrete stairs.
"L-Like I said, hang on, wai…!"
"Just a little further. Do your best, Haruki."
"Just a little further for what… Ah."
And once at the top of the stairs, I look up to find…
"Just as massive, pretentious, and completely lacking in any trace of culture as ever."
"I see… Come to think of it, it was in this part of town."
Onjuku Art and Culture Hall.
"Hm? Do you know this place, Haruki? I seem to remember you not showing up even once."
"Ugh…"
Yes, this is where Touma Kazusa held her first concert in Japan.
And this is where she held her additional concert a month later.
"I played here twice, yet you didn't come to listen even once."
"Well, that's because… I'm sorry, it was all my fault."
Tickets for both concerts sold out immediately, and the additional concert is still regarded as a legendary performance.
But despite the weight these performances held, I never set foot in the concert hall in the end.
"It's fine, already."
"But…"
"Because… it's thanks to the fact that you didn't show up, that we are together right now."
"…Yeah, you're right."
There is no point in theorizing about what could've been in a potential future that never happened.
Because now, I'm together with Kazusa.
And I've managed to return to the country I once abandoned.
At this point, there is nothing else I could ask for, and I wouldn't settle for anything different either.
"By the way, mom once held a concert here too."
"Yeah, I know."
I even got tickets for it, but I didn't go that time either…
"Though it didn't make the rounds nearly as much as my concert."
"You can reach a conclusion about that evaluation with your mother next time, without anyone else around."
The clock is nearing 10 PM.
We've spent the whole day just walking around.
Not once getting on a bus or a train, only walking around the streets of Onjuku with nothing but our memories to guide us.
But in that last place…
Just a road away from the way back to the hotel. In front of the station. Near the taxi stand.
Our feet stopped naturally, and our chatter died out.
"…Hey."
"Hm?"
"What are you thinking about?"
"Nothing…"
"Liar."
Wry smiles surface on our faces.
Our expressions are so pained, twisted, and distant that if someone looked at us they couldn't confidently say that we're smiling.
"We acted like idiots back then… didn't we?"
"Correction: we actually were idiots. We were half-witted beyond belief."
It was never my intention to come here.
This was the one place that I wanted to avoid. This place filled with so much nostalgia and pain.
"…Heh."
"Why are you laughing all of a sudden?"
"Because, because… even when I recall it now… Haha, hahaha…"
"Don't laugh."
"You said those exact same words back then too, with a tearful voice no less… Hahaha…!"
"And weren't you laughing and crying at the same time?"
"Ahahaha… Don't remind me."
"Haha…"
Yes, this is the place where both of us shed so many tears.
This is where we've shared so many of our first experiences.
This was where we had a serious quarrel for the first time.
This was where I struck her with my true feelings for the first time.
This was where Kazusa admitted her own true feelings for the first time.
And…
"Hey."
"Hm?"
"I said, hey."
"Yes, what do you wan…"
We were both looking toward the road together, but when I turned my head… I found her gaze already firmly set on me.
No, she wasn't simply gazing at me…
"Mh."
"Hey…"
She wanted me.
"You're more used to it now than back then, right? …Because of me."
"Why are you so used to it!?"
This is where our lips touched for the first time…
Actually, that was the second time, though I'd only figured that out much later after the fact.
Those times were filled with nothing but mistakes…
But even so, that was where our relationship started. It was from then on that we were able to share our feelings with one another.
"So… let's do it one more time here."
"Everyone's looking."
"They were looking back then too. But you still did it."
"I was young."
"You're still plenty young. So, Haruki…"
"Don't beg for things like a child. Act your age, would you?"
"What's that supposed to mean, I'm actually still… Mmmh!? Mhn… aah…"
"Mh, nh… Kazusa…!"
"H-Haru… Mhmm, nh, chu…"
And just like that…
With the passers-by and cars still firmly within the corners of our vision…
We share a kiss passionate enough to make every one of them turn their faces away.
Right hereーat the very place where we became accomplices for the first time.
